experiment.title: Zero identity, zero knowledge, zero actor trust, artifact-first trust, and genetic Rust backtrace
experiment.question: Can bounded predicates support hidden witnesses and minimized identity disclosure while artifact trust moves forward through developmental claim space and child Rust moves backward to concentrate on candidate falsehoods in bound ancestor claim architecture, without actor reputation becoming verdict weight?

hypotheses.statement: A real proof can establish the fixed experiment predicate without publishing the private witness bytes.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: The accepted public artifacts disclose the witness bytes or a documented verifier accepts a proof not bound to the fixed predicate and program identifier.

hypotheses.statement: The bounded identity evaluator preserves UNKNOWN and CONFLICTED rather than inferring uniqueness, independence, or authorization from absent identity information.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: A fixture with absent or contradictory identity evidence produces an unqualified accepted identity inference.

hypotheses.statement: Reverification can reproduce a verdict over bound public coordinates without accumulating actor reputation or historical trust.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: The proposed substrate requires actor identity or prior reputation to reproduce the bounded verdict, or repeated identical receipts increase epistemic strength without new evidence.

hypotheses.statement: Reverification acceptance is derived from bound artifacts, evidence, predicates, mechanisms, and declared trust roots; actor identity, popularity, repetition, or reputation cannot strengthen the verdict.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Changing only actor identity or reputation changes acceptance, repeated equivalent actor events raise status, or an unbound artifact is accepted.

hypotheses.statement: Actor and artifact are contextual roles on creation and operation events, so a coding agent may be an artifact when created or evaluated and an actor when it creates or transforms another artifact.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: The model requires permanent disjoint actor and artifact categories, loses a claim-relevant creation edge, or treats a role assignment as identity, authority, or trust.

hypotheses.statement: Observed child deviation transfers typed Rust backward through admissible bound creation paths, concentrating independent backtraces on shared ancestor claims, predicates, mechanisms, artifacts, and contextual coding-agent roles.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Rust cannot reproduce its child-to-ancestor paths, fails to concentrate distinct comparable sources, crosses non-contributing edges, or reports concentration as direct observation, proven causation, actor reputation, or a VSTD verdict.

hypotheses.statement: The bound development graph can carry scoped positive artifact trust from parent to child and diagnostic Rust from child to parent without collapsing them into one scalar or allowing either direction to bypass claim-local evidence.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: Positive support flows backward, Rust flows forward as inherited guilt, parent trust automatically proves a child, missing or conflicted support becomes clean, or actor identity changes either signal.

limitations: Round 2 is a design synthesis rather than a completed trustless protocol.
The zero-identity study is semantic and does not itself provide cryptographic anonymity or unlinkability.

actions.target: fixed hidden-evidence predicate and public VSTD-facing coordinates
actions.selected_because: A zero-knowledge claim required a real proof and independent verification rather than a commitment-only or development-mode substitute.
actions.expected_artifact_effect: Produce a bounded claim report and real proof implementation without changing core VSTD receipts.

actions.target: identity minimization, authorization boundaries, ancestry, and prohibited inferences
actions.selected_because: Identity minimization needed explicit negative fixtures before any operational protocol could be justified.
actions.expected_artifact_effect: Expose UNKNOWN, CONFLICTED, and rejected identity inferences in a reproducible fixture corpus.

actions.target: dual-direction artifact-first reverification: forward bounded artifact trust and backward genetic Rust concentration across contextual actor/artifact roles
actions.selected_because: The proof and identity studies exposed the need for artifact-first positive support without actor reputation, while coding-agent creation semantics require child-to-parent diagnostic Rust over the same causal graph.
alternatives_considered: object-only Rust with erased actor-artifact relations
permanent disjoint actor and artifact categories
actions.expected_artifact_effect: Define contextual roles, forward scoped artifact support, backward typed Rust transfer, and concentration at shared candidate ancestor falsehoods while leaving the operational protocol and schema open.

observations.statement: The recorded round-1 run generated and independently verified one real RISC Zero receipt and exercised the declared negative cases.
limitations: The committed report is the bound public record; generated private witness and local proof artifacts are intentionally excluded.

observations.statement: The recorded fixture suite preserved bounded acceptance, rejection, UNKNOWN, and CONFLICTED outcomes across the declared cases.
limitations: Semantic fixture behavior is not a cryptographic privacy, anonymity, authorization, or Sybil-resistance guarantee.

mapping.reason: The proof engine's native result is recorded without inventing a VSTD receipt mapping.
Fixture validation is preserved as its native result and does not become a core VSTD verdict.

adaptations.decision: Use one bound development graph for two typed directions: artifact trust moves parent-to-child as scoped positive support, and Rust moves child-to-parent as a genetic backtrace that concentrates on shared candidate falsehoods; neither becomes actor reputation or a scalar verdict.
adaptations.reason: Creation causality and diagnostic causality require opposite traversal of the same actor-artifact relations. Keeping both signals typed preserves the causal model without letting parent trust prove a child or inherited Rust claim direct guilt.

amendments.reason: Round 1 findings narrowed the design from identity-bound trust to artifact-bound trustless reverification.

Correct the object-only framing with contextual actor/artifact roles and dual causal propagation: bounded artifact trust moves forward through claim development, while child Rust genetically backtraces and concentrates on shared ancestor claim architecture without becoming actor reputation.

horizons.reason: Round 2 records a design substrate; no complete operational protocol or independent implementation is included.
Neither experiment establishes anonymity, unlinkability, identity uniqueness, or resistance to correlation outside its declared predicate.

horizons.reason: The design requires meet-like bounded support and child-local obligations, but no transfer algebra or implementation is included.
